accept: castel del monte bombino nero castel del monte nero di troia riserva castel del monte rosso riserva and primitivo di manduria dolce naturale
three castel del monte docgs plus primitivo di manduria dolce naturale
castel del monte bombino nero and primitivo di manduria dolce naturale
bombino nero rosato nero di troia riserva rosso riserva dolce naturale
ans: Castel del Monte Bombino Nero, Castel del Monte Nero di Troia Riserva, Castel del Monte Rosso Riserva, and Primitivo di Manduria Dolce Naturale.
exp: All four were elevated in 2011, which is why they are so often missed. Castel del Monte Bombino Nero is a rosato DOCG - Italy's only one - and that is the fact most likely to be asked. Note equally what is not DOCG: Primitivo di Manduria itself, Salice Salentino, Copertino and Gioia del Colle are all DOC, so the sweet Dolce Naturale sits above the dry wine that made the zone famous.

q: Marsala Vergine (Soleras) is set apart from the Oro, Ambra and Rubino Superiore categories because it:
opts: Carries no mosto cotto, sifone or other sweetening
Must be cask-aged for at least two years before sale
Must be made entirely from Grillo grown near Marsala
Is the only Marsala permitted to be labelled secco
exp: Vergine is the dry, unsweetened Marsala: nothing but fortified base wine and time, with a minimum of five years in wood - ten for Vergine Stravecchio or Riserva, so option 2 states Superiore's figure, not Vergine's. The sweetening agents are what give commercial Marsala its trolley-cart character: mosto cotto, cooked must, permitted only in Ambra, and sifone, a mistella of dried-grape must arrested with spirit. Vergine may use any of the permitted white varieties, not Grillo alone, and secco is a sweetness class available to the other categories too.

q: Name Barolo's two broad soil zones and the stylistic split they create.
accept: la morra barolo softer serralunga monforte sterner
ans: Tortonian marls (La Morra, Barolo: perfumed, earlier) vs Serravallian/Helvetian sandstone (Serralunga, Monforte: sterner, longer-lived)
exp: The exam wants the geologic names and a village for each.

q: What does 'MGA' stand for on a modern Barolo label?
ans: Menzione Geografica Aggiuntiva — the delimited cru names (181 in Barolo)
exp: Codified 2010; Barbaresco did it first (66 MGAs, 2007).

q: Match the Barolo MGA to its commune.
ans: Cannubi–Barolo · Brunate–La Morra · Vigna Rionda–Serralunga · Bussia–Monforte

q: Which producer's 'Sorì San Lorenzo', 'Sorì Tildìn' and 'Costa Russi' redefined single-vineyard Barbaresco?
exp: He later declassified them to Langhe DOC to blend in Barbera — reversed in 2013.

q: Besides Barbaresco and Neive, which is the other key commune of Barbaresco DOCG?
exp: Plus a sliver of Alba (San Rocco Seno d'Elvio).

q: The Produttori del Barbaresco bottles how many single-MGA riservas in top years?
exp: Nine (Asili, Rabajà, Ovello, etc.) — the world's finest co-op, founded 1958 on 1894 roots.

q: Gattinara and Ghemme build on Nebbiolo under what local name, with what supporting grapes?
ans: Spanna, with Vespolina and Uva Rara (Bonarda di Gattinara)
exp: Alto Piemonte's volcanic and glacial soils; Roberto Conterno of Giacomo Conterno bought Gattinara's Nervi estate in 2018 — now Nervi-Conterno.

q: Amarone della Valpolicella Riserva requires what minimum aging?
exp: 4 years (standard Amarone: 2, from Jan 1 after harvest); Recioto is the sweet parent style.

q: Which Soave subzone term marks the historic volcanic hills, and which producer's Calvarino and La Rocca define it?
exp: Calvarino sits on basalt, La Rocca on limestone below the Soave castle — the Classico hills hold both; Anselmi left the DOC in protest at its plains expansion.

q: Prosecco's DOCG pyramid tops out in which subzone famed for 'rive' and Cartizze?
ans: Conegliano-Valdobbiadene DOCG; 43 'Rive' plus Superiore di Cartizze
exp: Rive = single-commune steep parcels; Cartizze ~107 ha of gold.

q: Which Friulian DOCG for a dry white blend did Livio Felluga's 'Terre Alte' make famous, and which three grapes build it?
exp: Collio and Colli Orientali carry Friuli's white prestige; Gravner and Radikon took the amphora road nearby.

q: Ribolla Gialla macerated months in buried qvevri is the signature of which Oslavia producer?
exp: Orange wine's modern patriarch; Radikon and Prinčič share the hill.

q: Lambrusco's darkest, most tannic DOC, grown on the hills south of Modena, is Lambrusco:
exp: Grasparossa: dark, grippy, for gnocco fritto. Sorbara: palest, most acid-etched.
